meta.titre: Organic Nutrients: comparing carbohydrates, proteins and lipids
meta.sous_theme: Composition, building units and functions of the three major organic nutrients

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: At a roadside stall in Mile 17, Buea, a plate of cassava, beans and a spoonful of red palm oil is a full meal, yet it holds three different kinds of organic nutrient. The GCE asks you to name the elements in each class, to give the small units from which each is built, and to give functions and examples. These are easy marks if you keep the three classes separate in your head and in your answer, and they are lost quickly when carbohydrates, proteins and lipids are mixed up. This lesson gives you a clear comparison you can reproduce in a table or in short notes.

items: Food is digested into small soluble molecules that are absorbed into the blood.
Atoms of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen join to form the molecules of living things.
Water and mineral salts are inorganic substances because they are not built around carbon chains made by living organisms.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What organic means
Organic nutrients are carbon compounds made by living things. The three needed in large amounts are **carbohydrates**, **proteins** and **lipids** (fats and oils). Vitamins are also organic but are needed in tiny amounts.

### Comparison table
| | Carbohydrates | Proteins | Lipids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Elements | carbon, hydrogen, oxygen (hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2 : 1) | carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, often sulphur | carbon, hydrogen, oxygen (much less oxygen than in carbohydrates) |
| Building units | simple sugars (monosaccharides) such as glucose | amino acids, joined by peptide bonds | one glycerol joined to three fatty acids |
| Examples | glucose, sucrose, starch, glycogen, cellulose | egg white, meat, fish, beans, enzymes, haemoglobin | palm oil, groundnut oil, butter, animal fat |
| Main functions | quick source of energy; stored as glycogen in liver and muscles; cellulose gives fibre | growth and repair of tissues; making enzymes, hormones and antibodies | energy store and energy source; insulation under the skin; protection of organs; solvent for vitamins A, D, E and K |

### Larger molecules
Starch, glycogen and cellulose are **polysaccharides**: long chains of glucose units. Sucrose is a double sugar made of glucose joined to fructose. A protein is a long chain of many amino acids, and the order of the amino acids gives each protein its own shape and job.

### During digestion
Starch is broken down to glucose, proteins to amino acids, and fats to fatty acids and glycerol.

### Answering a 'short notes' question
Use one short paragraph per class and always follow the same order: composition, building unit, function(s), example. Examiners award a mark for each of these items, so never leave one out.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to compare classes of food or to show how they differ
variantes.contenu_markdown: Draw a table with the classes as columns and the headings (elements, building units, functions, examples) as rows. Write a similarity (all contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen) and then the differences (only proteins contain nitrogen; lipids give more energy per gram than carbohydrates).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question names a job and asks for the class of food responsible
variantes.contenu_markdown: Growth and repair: proteins. Quick energy: carbohydrates. Concentrated energy store and insulation: lipids. Regulation of body processes through enzymes and some hormones: proteins. Fibre for movement of food in the gut: cellulose, a carbohydrate.

sections.enonce_markdown: Compare carbohydrates and lipids under four headings: elements present, building units, one function and one named example of each. *(8 marks)*

etapes.action: Read the command word and plan the layout
etapes.justification: 'Compare' needs both classes dealt with side by side, so a table with four rows is the most efficient answer.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Columns: carbohydrates and lipids. Rows: elements, building units, function, example.

etapes.justification: Both contain the same three elements, which is a similarity worth stating, but their proportions differ.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Both: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen. Carbohydrates have hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2 : 1; lipids have much less oxygen.

etapes.justification: The units are different, so this row shows a clear difference.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Carbohydrates: simple sugars such as glucose. Lipids: glycerol and fatty acids.

etapes.action: Write a function and an example for each
etapes.justification: One function and one named example are asked for, so give exactly one of each, clearly worded.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Carbohydrates: quick source of energy, example starch (from yam). Lipids: store of energy and insulation under the skin, example palm oil.

etapes.justification: A short closing sentence shows the examiner that you understand the difference and not only the facts.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Gram for gram, lipids release more than twice as much energy as carbohydrates, so the body stores energy mainly as fat.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
| | Carbohydrates | Lipids |
|---|---|---|
| Elements | C, H, O (H : O is 2 : 1) | C, H, O (less oxygen) |
| Building units | simple sugars such as glucose | glycerol and fatty acids |
| Function | quick source of energy | energy store and insulation |
| Example | starch | palm oil |

Both classes contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only. Gram for gram, lipids give more than twice as much energy as carbohydrates.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that proteins are the body's main source of energy.
items.pourquoi_faux: The body uses carbohydrates first for energy. Proteins are used for energy only when carbohydrates and fats run short, and their main jobs are growth, repair and making enzymes.
items.correction_markdown: Carbohydrates are the main and quickest source of energy; proteins are for growth and repair.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that lipids are made of glucose, or that proteins are made of fatty acids.
items.pourquoi_faux: Each class has its own building units. Mixing them shows that the classes have not been learned separately.
items.correction_markdown: Carbohydrates: simple sugars. Proteins: amino acids. Lipids: glycerol and fatty acids.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing water and mineral salts as organic nutrients.
items.pourquoi_faux: Water and mineral salts are inorganic substances. They are not carbon compounds built by living organisms.
items.correction_markdown: Organic: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins. Inorganic: water, mineral salts.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving only a food as the example of a class, for instance 'protein: meat' or 'carbohydrate: rice'.
items.pourquoi_faux: A food is a mixture of several substances. The question asks for an example of the nutrient itself, and naming the compound earns the mark.
items.correction_markdown: Name the compound and, if you wish, its source: starch (in yam), albumin (in egg white), a triglyceride such as the oil in palm fruit.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that starch is a simple sugar.
items.pourquoi_faux: Starch is a polysaccharide made of very many glucose units. Simple sugars are the single units such as glucose and fructose.
items.correction_markdown: Starch: polysaccharide made of glucose units. Glucose: simple sugar.

|---|---|---|
| Cassava | | |

items.solution_markdown:
| Food | Main nutrient | One use in the body |
|---|---|---|
| Cassava | carbohydrate (starch) | supplies energy |
| Fish | protein | growth and repair of tissues |
| Red palm oil | lipid | energy store, or solvent for vitamins A, D, E and K |
| Egg white | protein | growth and repair of tissues, or making enzymes |

**Cassava: carbohydrate; fish: protein; palm oil: lipid; egg white: protein.**

items.enonce_markdown: A breakfast contains 50 g of carbohydrate, 10 g of protein and 12 g of lipid. Use the energy values of 17 kJ per gram for carbohydrate and for protein and 37 kJ per gram for lipid. (a) Calculate the energy released by each nutrient and the total energy of the breakfast. (b) Calculate the percentage of the total energy that comes from lipid, to one decimal place. (c) Which nutrient supplies most of the energy?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Energy = mass $\times$ energy value.

Carbohydrate: $50 \times 17 = 850$ kJ. Protein: $10 \times 17 = 170$ kJ. Lipid: $12 \times 37 = 444$ kJ.

Total: $850 + 170 + 444 = 1464$ kJ. **Total energy = 1464 kJ.**

(b) Percentage from lipid $= \frac{444}{1464} \times 100 = 30.3\%$. **30.3 %.**

(c) Carbohydrate gives 850 kJ, which is the largest share (58.1 %). **Carbohydrate.**

items.enonce_markdown: A young child is fed almost only on boiled cassava. After some months the child has a swollen abdomen, thin arms and legs, and grows slowly. (a) Name the deficiency disease and the nutrient that is lacking. (b) Explain why the lack of this nutrient affects growth. (c) Suggest two foods that could be added to the diet to correct the problem. (d) Why does the child still have plenty of energy in the diet even though it is ill?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The disease is **kwashiorkor**, caused by a lack of **protein**.

(b) Proteins are made of amino acids, which the body uses to build new cells and to repair damaged tissues. Without enough amino acids, cells cannot be made, so growth is slow and muscles waste away. Proteins are also needed to make enzymes, antibodies and haemoglobin, so the child also falls ill easily.

(c) Any two protein-rich foods, for example beans, fish, eggs, groundnuts, milk or meat.

(d) Cassava is rich in starch, a carbohydrate, which releases energy. The diet lacks protein, not energy. **The missing nutrient is protein.**

items_markdown: Carbohydrates, proteins and lipids are the three major organic nutrients; water and mineral salts are inorganic.
Carbohydrates contain C, H and O and are built from simple sugars; proteins also contain N and are built from amino acids; lipids contain C, H and O and are built from glycerol and fatty acids.
Carbohydrates give quick energy, proteins give growth and repair, and lipids store energy and insulate the body.
Gram for gram, lipids release more than twice the energy of carbohydrates.
In a short-notes answer, always give composition, building unit, function and example in that order, with a named compound as the example.
